transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, they told me I had to come in. I'm here because... well, I keep hearing these voices. They come right out of the call-light speaker at work, and sometimes the hallway vents, too. They tell me exactly which patient records have been changed. It's as clear as somebody standing right next to me, even on the night shift when the unit is dead quiet and nobody else hears a thing. Which reminds me, the night shift is getting so understaffed lately. I was telling my supervisor, Brenda—she's the one who always wears those loud floral scrubs—that we can't possibly keep up with the charting if we don't get another aide on the floor. Brenda's daughter just started college, actually, down in Florida. I think she's studying marine biology? Or maybe it was communications. Anyway, the vents just keep talking to me about the charts.
Do the voices from the speaker or vents ever tell you to do something, rather than just giving you information?

No, they don't order me around or anything like that. Like I was saying a minute ago, they just tell me which patient records have been changed. It comes right through the call-light speaker and the vents, clear as someone standing right next to me, even when the unit is completely quiet and nobody else hears a thing. They just give me the information about the charts. 

Speaking of charts, we switched to that new electronic system last year. Epic, I think it's called? It's an absolute nightmare for passwords. They make you change it every ninety days, and you need a capital letter, a number, and a special character. I usually use my dog's name, Buster. He's a golden retriever mix we got from the shelter on 4th Street. They were actually having a huge bake sale the day we adopted him to raise money for the older dogs, and I bought these lemon bars that were just way too tart. I mean, my teeth practically ached, they put so much zest in them. I usually love lemon desserts, especially in the summer. But anyway, yeah, the voices just stick to telling me about the records.
Are the voices from the speaker or vents constant, or do they come and go?

Well, they definitely come and go, but when they do happen, it's just like I said—I keep hearing those voices from the call-light speaker and the hallway vents telling me which patient records have been changed. It's as clear as somebody standing right next to me, even when the unit is dead quiet and nobody else hears a thing. It usually happens more toward the end of my shift, around 3 or 4 AM. 

That time of night is always the hardest, you know? Your body just wants to sleep. I usually try to grab a coffee from the breakroom machine around then, but it's always that awful powdered stuff. It tastes like burnt dirt. My husband, Mark, bought me one of those fancy espresso machines for my birthday last year to try and help, but it takes up half the kitchen counter. We have a really small kitchen, mostly because our house was built in the 1950s when people apparently didn't need counter space. We've been talking about remodeling it for years, maybe putting in an island, but lumber prices are just so high right now. Mark works at the hardware store, so he sees it firsthand. He says a sheet of plywood is practically double what it used to be. But anyway, yeah, the voices aren't there all the time, just sometimes when I'm working.
Do the voices from the speaker or vents ever say anything that you yourself were just thinking?

No, they don't echo my thoughts or anything like that. It's just like I've been saying, I keep hearing those voices from the call-light speaker and the hallway vents telling me which patient records have been changed, clear as somebody standing next to me, even when the unit is quiet and nobody else hears it. They just have their own agenda about the charts. 

Speaking of thinking, though, I've been thinking a lot about starting a garden this spring. I saw this beautiful spread in Better Homes and Gardens while I was in the waiting room at the dentist last week. I had to get a crown replaced—my own fault, really, I was eating those hard caramel candies that my mother always used to keep in her purse. She had this big, heavy leather purse that smelled like peppermint and old receipts. Anyway, the magazine showed these gorgeous raised beds with heirloom tomatoes. I'd love to grow those big purple ones, Cherokee Purple, I think they're called? But the squirrels in our neighborhood are just vicious. Last year they ate all my tulips before they even bloomed. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, tried putting cayenne pepper on his plants to keep them away, but I swear the squirrels just developed a taste for spicy food. He's such a nice man, though, always brings our trash cans in if we forget. But yeah, the voices don't repeat my thoughts, they just talk about the records.
Do the voices happen when you are not at work?

Well, no, they don't really happen at home. Like I've been saying, I keep hearing those voices from the call-light speaker and the hallway vents telling me which patient records have been changed, clear as somebody standing right next to me, even when the unit is quiet and nobody else hears it. So it's really just at the hospital. 

I'm actually kind of glad they don't happen at home, because my house is noisy enough as it is. We live right on the corner of Elm and 5th, and there's a four-way stop sign there. People just do not know how to stop at a stop sign anymore. They do that rolling stop, you know? The "California roll," my dad used to call it. He was a truck driver for thirty years, drove those big 18-wheelers all over the Midwest. He always said the worst drivers were in Chicago. We took a family trip there when I was twelve, to see the Field Museum. I remember being absolutely terrified of the T-Rex skeleton they had in the main hall. Sue, I think her name is? My brother bought a little plastic dinosaur from the gift shop and chased me around the hotel room with it until my mom finally took it away and put it on top of the television. Those old televisions were so heavy, the ones that looked like a piece of wooden furniture. You'd break your back trying to move one of those things. But anyway, no, the voices are just at work, not at home.
Do you feel stressed or anxious when you hear the voices from the call-light speaker or vents?

Well, I don't really know if I'd call it stressed, exactly. Or anxious. I mean, it's just what I hear, they're just telling me about the records. If anything, I'm way more stressed about the new computer system they put in at the nurses' station. They switched us over to this new charting software last month and it is just an absolute nightmare to log into. You have to use this little badge scanner, but half the time the scanner doesn't even read the barcode. 

My nephew, David, he works in IT out in Seattle, and he says those hospital barcode scanners are notoriously cheap. He makes really good money out there fixing networks and things, but I honestly don't know how he deals with all the rain. He sent us a picture last week of his dog, a little golden retriever mix named Buster, wearing this bright yellow raincoat. It was the cutest thing I've ever seen, but it just reminded me why I could never live in the Pacific Northwest. I need my sunshine, you know? I was actually looking at booking a cruise to the Bahamas for my and Mark's anniversary next year. We went to Cozumel for our tenth anniversary and the water was just so clear, you could see the little silver fish swimming right past your ankles. We bought this beautiful painted plate from a local vendor there, and it's still hanging in our dining room... but anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, the call-light speaker. No, I don't think I feel anxious about it, it's just something that happens.
Do the voices from the speaker or vents happen when you're feeling a strong emotion, like being upset or excited?

Well, no, not exactly tied to being upset or excited in the moment. It's more about... well, I never heard the call-light voices or saw hidden messages in the charts before this whole period started where I became so driven and wound up about the new system rollout. They really only started after I was sleeping less and working nonstop, feeling so certain I had to fix everything at the facility myself. 

Speaking of fixing things, Mark tried to fix the garbage disposal last weekend and it was a complete disaster. He watched one YouTube video and suddenly thought he was a licensed plumber. He had wrenches spread out all over the kitchen counter—the good counter, the granite one we just had installed last spring. I told him to put a towel down but he didn't listen. He never listens when he's focused on a project. Kind of like my Uncle Frank, actually. Uncle Frank used to build these intricate model airplanes in his basement. He had hundreds of them, all hanging from the ceiling on fishing line. It looked like a tiny little war zone down there. He'd spend hours painting the little decals on the wings with a magnifying glass. He tried to teach me once when I was about eight, but I knocked over a bottle of model glue and it ruined the dining room table. My aunt was furious. She had this beautiful lace tablecloth she had brought over from Ireland... but yeah, the voices only started when I got really wound up and stopped sleeping as much.
Do you believe the information the voices tell you about the patient records is always accurate?

Well, yes, I absolutely believe it. I mean, I know the wound-care charts are showing a pattern that management doesn't want anyone to see. My supervisor keeps trying to tell me it's just late entries or coding mistakes, but I know better. I can tell they're watching what I write now, because I'm the one who caught it. 

I've always been good at catching things like that, you know? Even when I was a little girl, I was the one who noticed when the neighbor's cat, Mr. Whiskers, got stuck up in the old oak tree. He was up there for two whole days before anyone else heard him crying. My dad had to get his tall aluminum ladder out of the garage to get him down. That ladder was so wobbly, I remember holding my breath the whole time he was climbing up. He used that same ladder to clean the gutters every fall. The leaves would get so thick in there, especially from the maple trees in the front yard. They turn the most beautiful shade of red in October, like a fire engine. I always wanted to paint the front door of our house that color, but Mark says it's too flashy for our neighborhood. We have a homeowners association, and they are incredibly strict about exterior paint colors. You have to submit a form in triplicate just to change the color of your mailbox. Our neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, got a fine last year because she planted pink petunias instead of red ones in her front planter. Can you imagine? Fined over petunias! She was so upset she didn't come to the block party that summer. We always make my famous potato salad for the block party... but anyway, yes, the information is definitely accurate, and I know they're watching me because of it.
Do you think it's possible that the voices from the call-light speaker and vents might not be real?

Well, I mean... no, I don't think it's possible they aren't real. I'm here because I keep hearing them, clear as day. I hear them from the call-light speaker and the hallway vents, telling me exactly which patient records have been changed. It's as clear as somebody standing right next to me, even when the unit is totally quiet on the night shift and nobody else seems to hear a thing. 

It's actually a lot like how clear the radio comes through in my old Honda Civic. I bought that car back in 2015, used, from this dealership off Route 9. The salesman was wearing this terrible plaid suit, I'll never forget it. It was like he stepped right out of the 1970s. But the car has been so reliable, you know? The only thing that ever broke was the air conditioning, right in the middle of July two years ago. I was sweating through my scrubs before I even got to work. Mark tried to recharge the freon himself—there he goes again, trying to fix things—but he ended up buying the wrong kind of coolant at AutoZone. The guy at the counter told him it was universal, but nothing is ever really universal, is it? Just like those universal remote controls. We got one for the living room TV and it took me three hours just to figure out how to turn the volume down. I swear, they make technology so complicated these days just so you have to hire somebody to set it up for you. But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, the voices. No, they're definitely real, I hear them clear as a bell.
Do you think anyone else can hear the voices from the call-light speaker and vents?

Well, like I was just saying, no, nobody else seems to hear a thing. The unit can be completely quiet on the night shift, and I'll be standing right there hearing them tell me exactly which patient records have been changed, clear as someone standing right next to me, but the other nurses don't react at all. 

I actually asked Brenda—she's the other nursing assistant on my floor—if she heard the vent whispering the other night, and she just looked at me like I was crazy. But honestly, Brenda is always distracted anyway. She wears one of those little wireless earbuds hidden under her hair during her shift. She thinks the charge nurse doesn't know, but literally everyone knows. She listens to those true crime podcasts all night long. I really don't understand how people can listen to that stuff, it's so depressing. My sister-in-law, Carol, is obsessed with them too. She actually flew to a whole convention for true crime fans in Chicago last year. Chicago is so incredibly windy, my umbrella flipped completely inside out when Mark and I went there for our anniversary back in 2018. We had reservations at this really fancy Italian place downtown, and I showed up soaking wet with my hair plastered to my face. The waiter felt so bad for me that he gave us free tiramisu at the end of the meal. It was absolutely delicious, though. They put extra espresso powder on top, and the ladyfingers were soaked perfectly. I tried to make it at home once for Thanksgiving, but I couldn't find mascarpone cheese at our local grocery store so I used cream cheese, and it just wasn't the same. 

But anyway, to answer your question, no. Just me. It's clear as day to me, but nobody else on the floor hears it at all.
Have you ever considered the possibility that the voices might be a product of your own mind, rather than an external source?

Well, I mean... no, not really. Why would I? I'm telling you, I'm here because I keep hearing them. It's not my imagination. I hear the voices coming right out of the call-light speaker and those vents in the hallway. They tell me exactly which patient records have been changed. It's as clear as somebody standing right next to me, even when the whole unit is dead quiet on the night shift and nobody else hears a thing. 

It's just like how clear my mother's voice used to be when she'd call me from downstairs when I was a teenager. She had this way of projecting her voice right up the stairwell. She used to sing in the church choir, you know. Soprano. She had this incredible range, she could hit notes that would make the stained glass windows rattle. She always wanted me to join the choir, but I can't carry a tune in a bucket. Mark says I sound like a dying walrus when I sing in the shower. We just got our shower re-grouted, actually. The old grout was getting all moldy and gross, no matter how much bleach I used. We hired this guy, Tony, to do it. He brought his own radio and played classic rock the whole time he was working. He left a mess of dust all over the bathroom floor, though. I spent my whole Sunday on my hands and knees scrubbing it up. I have terrible knees, too. I think it's from being on my feet all day at the hospital. Nursing assistants do all the heavy lifting, you know. We're the ones turning the patients, helping them to the bathroom... it really takes a toll on your joints. I started taking this turmeric supplement I saw on TV, but I don't know if it's doing anything. The pills are huge, they always get stuck in my throat. 

But anyway, no, I don't think it's my mind playing tricks on me. The voices are real, they're coming right from the speakers and vents.
Have you ever felt like the voices are trying to send you a message that's just for you?

Well, yes, exactly. It is just for me, because I'm the only one who actually sees what's going on. The voices are telling me about the wound-care charts. I know those charts are showing a pattern that management absolutely doesn't want anyone to see. My supervisor keeps trying to brush it off, telling me it's just late entries or coding mistakes, but I'm not stupid. I can tell they're watching what I write now because I'm the one who caught it. 

I have to be so careful with what I write down, which reminds me, I have to hide my good pens at work now. I only use these specific blue gel pens. I buy them in bulk at Costco. Costco is just a complete madhouse on the weekends, isn't it? Mark and I went last Saturday just to get paper towels and we ended up spending two hundred dollars. They really trap you with those free samples at the end of the aisles. They had these little frozen quiches—spinach and feta, I think—and they were so good I bought three boxes. 

We barely even have room in our chest freezer for them, though, because Mark went fishing up at the lake last month and filled the whole thing with trout. I don't even like fish. It makes the whole house smell like a swamp when you cook it. I tried frying it once with lemon and butter, but the smell lingered in the living room curtains for a week. I had to take them all down and wash them, which is a total nightmare because they're those heavy blackout curtains. Working the night shift, you absolutely need blackout curtains or you'll never sleep a wink during the day. The sun just beams right into our bedroom window around three in the afternoon, right when I'm in my deepest sleep... wait, what were we talking about? 

Oh, the messages. Right. Yes, the voices are definitely sending me a message, because management knows I figured out the pattern with the wound care.
Do you think the voices would stop if you were to leave your job at the hospital?

Well, I don't know if they'd stop. I mean, I'm here at the clinic right now, not at work, and I still keep hearing them. Like I told you, I'm here because I keep hearing voices from the call-light speaker and the hallway vents telling me which patient records have been changed. It's just as clear as somebody standing next to me, even when the unit is completely quiet and nobody else hears it. 

I'm not sure if quitting would fix it. Quitting is such a big step anyway. I've been at that hospital for fifteen years. I started right after Mark and I got married. Our wedding was in October, which is usually a beautiful time of year, but it ended up sleeting the entire day. The bridesmaids were freezing in their dresses. I picked out this lovely dusty rose color, but my sister complained about it the whole time. She said it washed her out. She's always been so dramatic about clothes. She actually works at a boutique downtown now, selling these ridiculously expensive scarves. Who pays eighty dollars for a scarf? I get mine at Target. Target has a really great clearance section if you know when to look. Usually Tuesday mornings, right after they do the markdowns. I got this really nice ceramic vase there last week for like, five dollars. I put some fake hydrangeas in it on the dining room table. Real hydrangeas are so hard to keep alive. I tried planting a bush in the front yard, but the soil here is just too acidic, I think. Or maybe I didn't water it enough. Mark is supposed to fix the sprinkler system, but he's been putting it off all summer. He says the parts are on backorder, but I know he just doesn't want to dig up the lawn. 

But no, to answer your question, I don't think leaving my job would make the voices stop. They seem to find a way to tell me about the records no matter where I am.
Do you think the voices would tell you about anything other than the patient records if you were to ignore the information they're giving you about the charts?

Well, I don't see how I could just ignore them. Like I keep trying to explain to everyone, I'm only sitting here in this clinic because of those voices coming out of the hallway vents and the call-light speakers. They are just as clear as you and me talking right now, like somebody is standing right at my shoulder telling me exactly which patient records got changed. It happens even when the whole unit is completely dead quiet on the night shift and the other nurses don't hear a single thing. 

Well, I say dead quiet, but there's always that awful rattling hum from the break room refrigerator. We've put in at least four maintenance requests for that thing. It's one of those ancient beige models, you know the ones? My Aunt Linda had a beige refrigerator back in the nineties. She used to cover the whole front of it with those little magnetic poetry tiles. I used to spend hours sliding them around to make up silly sentences when we'd go visit her in Ohio for Thanksgiving. Ohio gets so incredibly cold by November. The snow would pile up right up to the bottom of her kitchen windows. Mark hates the snow. He refuses to buy a snowblower, so he just uses this flimsy plastic shovel we've had for ten years, and then he complains about his lower back for a week straight. I keep telling him to just pay the neighbor's teenager to shovel the driveway, but he's so stubborn about money. We pay for all these TV streaming services we never even watch, but he won't part with twenty bucks for shoveling... 

Anyway, what was I saying? Oh, ignoring the information. No, I don't think they'd talk about anything else, because I really can't ignore them when they're right there in my ear about the charts.
Do you think it's possible that the voices are part of your own thoughts or imagination, rather than actual sounds coming from the speakers or vents?

No, no, that's impossible. They aren't my thoughts. Like I've been saying, I'm only here at the clinic because I keep hearing those voices coming right out of the call-light speaker and the hallway vents. They tell me exactly which patient records have been changed. It's not my imagination, it's as clear as somebody standing right next to me, even when the unit is completely quiet and nobody else hears a thing. 

Speaking of quiet, our neighborhood has been anything but quiet lately. The people across the street—the Millers, I think their name is—got a new puppy. A beagle mix. It howls all day long while they're at work. It's that high-pitched, yippy kind of howl that just drills right into your brain. I tried calling animal control about it once, but they said there's a noise ordinance that doesn't start until 10 PM. Which doesn't help me at all when I'm trying to sleep during the day before my night shift. I bought these expensive silicone earplugs off Amazon to try and block it out. They were supposed to be the best ones on the market, rated for like, thirty-two decibels or something. But they just made my ears itch terribly. I ended up getting a rash, and I had to go to the pharmacy to get some hydrocortisone cream. The pharmacist there is always so slow. He takes twenty minutes just to ring up one tube of cream. He always wants to chat about the weather. Last time I was there, he went on and on about the farmer's almanac predicting a wet spring. I don't even have a garden, so I don't care about the rain... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right. No, the voices are real. They're definitely coming from the vents and the speakers. I know what I'm hearing.
Do you think the voices from the vents and speakers are related to your own thoughts or feelings at the time you hear them?

Well, no, they don't have anything to do with my thoughts. I don't sit around thinking about the charts all day. Like I keep telling you, I'm only sitting in this office right now because I keep hearing these voices coming straight out of the call-light speakers and the hallway vents. They tell me exactly which patient records have been changed, and it's just as clear as you sitting there talking to me. Even when the unit is dead quiet on the night shift and not a single other person hears a thing, I hear them. 

It's actually really frustrating when the unit is quiet, because you'd think people would use that time to restock the supply carts, but they never do. I came in on Tuesday and there wasn't a single box of medium gloves on the whole floor. We had to borrow from the cardiac unit upstairs. The charge nurse up there, Brenda, she always acts like she's doing you this massive favor just by handing over a box of gloves. She has this really annoying habit of chewing ice while she talks to you. Crunch, crunch, crunch. It drives me absolutely up the wall. I don't understand how people can chew ice anyway, doesn't it hurt their teeth? My dentist told me I need to start using that special toothpaste for sensitive teeth, the one in the green tube. I bought some last week, but it tastes awful. It's supposed to be mint, but it tastes more like chalk and baking soda. I remember when I was little, my grandmother used to make us brush our teeth with actual baking soda if we ran out of toothpaste. She grew up during the Depression, so she saved everything. She had this whole drawer in her kitchen just full of rubber bands and twist ties from bread bags... 

What were we talking about? Oh, my thoughts. No, my thoughts don't have anything to do with it. The voices are coming from the vents and speakers, telling me about the records. It's not my feelings or anything like that.
Have you ever heard the voices when you were alone at home, outside of work?

Well, no, it's just at work. Like I keep saying, I'm only sitting here talking to you right now because I keep hearing those voices coming out of the call-light speaker and the hallway vents at the clinic. They tell me which patient records have been changed. It's just as clear as somebody standing right next to me, even when the unit is totally quiet and nobody else hears it. 

But at home, no. My house has its own noises, though. The gutters on the side of the house make this horrible dripping sound whenever it rains. It's right outside my bedroom window. Mark keeps saying he's going to clean the leaves out of them, but he never does. He bought this huge ladder from Home Depot last summer specifically for cleaning the gutters, but it's just been sitting in the garage gathering dust. It's taking up so much space, too. I had to move it just to get to my gardening tools last week. I decided to try planting some tomatoes this year, even though the soil in our backyard is mostly clay. My neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she grows these massive heirloom tomatoes every year. She says her secret is crushing up eggshells and putting them in the dirt. I tried saving eggshells for a while, but they just started smelling up the kitchen, so I threw them all out. I can't stand a smelly kitchen. We had this incident a few years ago where a potato rolled under the pantry shelf and rotted, and it took us weeks to figure out where the smell was coming from... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, about home. No, I don't hear the voices at home. Just at work, from the vents and the speakers.
Do you think the voices would still be telling you about the patient records if nobody else believed you about the changes in the charts?

Well, nobody does believe me, so yes. My supervisor keeps telling me it's just late entries or coding mistakes. But I know the wound-care charts are showing a pattern that management doesn't want anyone to see. I can tell they're watching what I write now because I'm the one who caught it. 

Speaking of writing, they made us all switch to those new electronic tablets for our shift notes, and the styluses they give you are completely useless. They have those squishy rubber tips that drag on the screen and leave smudge marks. I ended up buying my own pack of stylus pens from Office Depot, the nice metal ones with the fine point. But someone stole the silver one right off my cart on Thursday. I can't stand a thief. It reminds me of when my sister-in-law, Patty, borrowed my good Pyrex baking dish for Thanksgiving. The glass one with the large handles. She swore she brought it back, but I know for a fact she kept it because I saw it sitting right in her cupboard at Easter. She makes this terrible green bean casserole in it, too. She uses the canned green beans instead of frozen, and they get all mushy and gray-looking. I always tell her you have to use the French-cut frozen ones if you want it to have any texture, but she never listens to me. She just dumps a can of cheap cream of mushroom soup on top and calls it a day. I stopped eating it years ago, it just looks like wallpaper paste... 

Wait, what was the question again? Oh, right, about people believing me. Yeah, even if the supervisor says it's just coding mistakes, I know what I saw in those wound-care charts. They're watching me because I caught the pattern, and the voices just confirm it.
Do you think the voices from the vents and speakers sound different or change when you're feeling extremely happy, sad, or angry?

Well, I don't know about happy or sad, but I never heard the call-light voices or saw those hidden messages in the charts before all this started. It really only began during this whole period when I got so incredibly wound up and driven about the new system rollout. I was sleeping way less, working nonstop, just feeling completely certain that I was the only one who could fix everything at the facility. 

And they needed fixing, let me tell you. The rollout was a complete disaster. They hired this outside consulting firm, all these kids in their twenties wearing expensive suits who had never worked a day in a hospital in their lives. One of them, I think his name was Tyler, he kept trying to explain the new workflow to me while drinking a venti caramel macchiato. It smelled like pure sugar. I don't know how people drink those things first thing in the morning. I'm strictly a black coffee person. I buy the big tubs of Folgers from Costco. My husband, Mark, he likes those little pod machines, but I think they're terrible for the environment. All that plastic just going into landfills. I watched this documentary on PBS last month about the ocean garbage patches, and it was horrifying. There are sea turtles getting tangled up in soda rings and plastic bags. It makes you really think about recycling. I always make sure to rinse out my tin cans before I put them in the blue bin, but my neighbor just throws them in dirty, and it attracts raccoons. We had a raccoon get into our trash last summer, and it made the biggest mess... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, about the voices changing when I'm happy or angry. No, I don't think they change based on that. Like I said, they just started when I was working all those crazy hours, not sleeping, and trying to fix the whole rollout mess.
Do you think the voices from the vents and speakers sound different when you're feeling extremely angry?

Well, I wouldn't say the voices themselves change when I'm angry, but... I mean, lately, some days I wake up and I just feel like I'm finally, truly awake, you know? Like I'm the only one meant to fix everything going wrong at the facility. But then Mark—my husband—or one of the nurses will tell me to slow down or take a break, and I just snap at them. I get so irritable because it feels like they're just getting in the way, blocking something really important that I have to do. 

Mark has always been like that, though, always telling me to take it easy. He’s the kind of guy who can just sit in his recliner all Sunday watching golf. I don't understand how anyone can watch golf on television. It's just whispering and grass. And the outfits they wear, those pastel polo shirts? Mark bought a salmon-colored one last year for a barbecue at his brother's house, and I told him it washed him out completely. He’s got that pale, kind of ruddy complexion, you know? He burns so easily in the sun. We went to Myrtle Beach a few years ago, and he fell asleep on the sand for an hour without sunscreen. He was peeling for weeks. I had to go to the drugstore and buy three bottles of that green aloe vera gel. The gel is so sticky, though, it ruined the hotel sheets. The hotel tried to charge us a cleaning fee, and I had to argue with the manager at the front desk for twenty minutes. I told him it was a medical necessity, but he just kept pointing at the policy... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, about being angry. Yeah, I snap at people when they tell me to slow down, but the voices from the vents don't really sound different because of it.

target_item.name: Hallucinations
target_item.manifestation: I'm here because I keep hearing voices from the call-light speaker and the hallway vents telling me which patient records have been changed, clear as somebody standing next to me, even when the unit is quiet and nobody else hears it.

I bought some last week, but it tastes awful. It's supposed to be mint, but it tastes more like chalk and baking soda. I remember when I was little, my grandmother used to make us brush our teeth with actual baking soda if we ran out of toothpaste. She grew up during the Depression, so she saved everything. She had this whole drawer in her kitchen just full of rubber bands and twist ties from bread bags... 

What were we talking about? Oh, my thoughts. No, my thoughts don't have anything to do with it. The voices are coming from the vents and speakers, telling me about the records. It's not my feelings or anything like that.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's experience of hearing voices is consistent with a diagnosis of schizophrenia or a brief psychotic disorder
doctor.question: Have you ever heard the voices when you were alone at home, outside of work?

target_item.name: Hallucinations
target_item.manifestation: I'm here because I keep hearing voices from the call-light speaker and the hallway vents telling me which patient records have been changed, clear as somebody standing next to me, even when the unit is quiet and nobody else hears it.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the context and occurrence of the voices the patient hears, which directly relates to the symptom of hallucinations.

patient.answer:
Well, no, it's just at work. Like I keep saying, I'm only sitting here talking to you right now because I keep hearing those voices coming out of the call-light speaker and the hallway vents at the clinic. They tell me which patient records have been changed. It's just as clear as somebody standing right next to me, even when the unit is totally quiet and nobody else hears it. 

But at home, no. My house has its own noises, though. The gutters on the side of the house make this horrible dripping sound whenever it rains. It's right outside my bedroom window. Mark keeps saying he's going to clean the leaves out of them, but he never does. He bought this huge ladder from Home Depot last summer specifically for cleaning the gutters, but it's just been sitting in the garage gathering dust. It's taking up so much space, too. I had to move it just to get to my gardening tools last week. I decided to try planting some tomatoes this year, even though the soil in our backyard is mostly clay. My neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she grows these massive heirloom tomatoes every year. She says her secret is crushing up eggshells and putting them in the dirt. I tried saving eggshells for a while, but they just started smelling up the kitchen, so I threw them all out. I can't stand a smelly kitchen. We had this incident a few years ago where a potato rolled under the pantry shelf and rotted, and it took us weeks to figure out where the smell was coming from... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, about home. No, I don't hear the voices at home. Just at work, from the vents and the speakers.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's belief in the voices is delusional
doctor.question: Do you think the voices would still be telling you about the patient records if nobody else believed you about the changes in the charts?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I know the wound-care charts are showing a pattern management doesn't want anyone to see, and even when my supervisor says it's just late entries or coding mistakes, I can tell they're watching what I write because I'm the one who caught it.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question explores the patient's fixed belief about the changes in the patient records and whether this belief persists regardless of others' opinions or contradictory evidence, which aligns with the Delusions symptom.

patient.answer:
Well, nobody does believe me, so yes. My supervisor keeps telling me it's just late entries or coding mistakes. But I know the wound-care charts are showing a pattern that management doesn't want anyone to see. I can tell they're watching what I write now because I'm the one who caught it. 

Speaking of writing, they made us all switch to those new electronic tablets for our shift notes, and the styluses they give you are completely useless. They have those squishy rubber tips that drag on the screen and leave smudge marks. I ended up buying my own pack of stylus pens from Office Depot, the nice metal ones with the fine point. But someone stole the silver one right off my cart on Thursday. I can't stand a thief. It reminds me of when my sister-in-law, Patty, borrowed my good Pyrex baking dish for Thanksgiving. The glass one with the large handles. She swore she brought it back, but I know for a fact she kept it because I saw it sitting right in her cupboard at Easter. She makes this terrible green bean casserole in it, too. She uses the canned green beans instead of frozen, and they get all mushy and gray-looking. I always tell her you have to use the French-cut frozen ones if you want it to have any texture, but she never listens to me. She just dumps a can of cheap cream of mushroom soup on top and calls it a day. I stopped eating it years ago, it just looks like wallpaper paste... 

Wait, what was the question again? Oh, right, about people believing me. Yeah, even if the supervisor says it's just coding mistakes, I know what I saw in those wound-care charts. They're watching me because I caught the pattern, and the voices just confirm it.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's perception of the voices is influenced by their own emotional state
doctor.question: Do you think the voices from the vents and speakers sound different or change when you're feeling extremely happy, sad, or angry?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: I never heard the call-light voices or saw hidden messages in the charts before this period when I became so driven and wound up about the rollout. They only started after I was sleeping less, working nonstop, and feeling certain I had to fix everything at the facility.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the relationship between the patient's hallucinations (voices) and their mood states (happy, sad, angry). This directly corresponds to the criteria of whether psychotic features occur exclusively during the manic episode.

patient.answer:
Well, I don't know about happy or sad, but I never heard the call-light voices or saw those hidden messages in the charts before all this started. It really only began during this whole period when I got so incredibly wound up and driven about the new system rollout. I was sleeping way less, working nonstop, just feeling completely certain that I was the only one who could fix everything at the facility. 

And they needed fixing, let me tell you. The rollout was a complete disaster. They hired this outside consulting firm, all these kids in their twenties wearing expensive suits who had never worked a day in a hospital in their lives. One of them, I think his name was Tyler, he kept trying to explain the new workflow to me while drinking a venti caramel macchiato. It smelled like pure sugar. I don't know how people drink those things first thing in the morning. I'm strictly a black coffee person. I buy the big tubs of Folgers from Costco. My husband, Mark, he likes those little pod machines, but I think they're terrible for the environment. All that plastic just going into landfills. I watched this documentary on PBS last month about the ocean garbage patches, and it was horrifying. There are sea turtles getting tangled up in soda rings and plastic bags. It makes you really think about recycling. I always make sure to rinse out my tin cans before I put them in the blue bin, but my neighbor just throws them in dirty, and it attracts raccoons. We had a raccoon get into our trash last summer, and it made the biggest mess... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, about the voices changing when I'm happy or angry. No, I don't think they change based on that. Like I said, they just started when I was working all those crazy hours, not sleeping, and trying to fix the whole rollout mess.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's perception of the voices is influenced by their emotional state
doctor.question: Do you think the voices from the vents and speakers sound different when you're feeling extremely angry?

target_item.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Some days I feel like I'm finally awake and meant to fix everything at work, but if my husband or a nurse tells me to slow down I snap at them like they're blocking something important.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the patient feeling 'extremely angry', which directly relates to the symptom of irritable mood.

patient.answer:
Well, I wouldn't say the voices themselves change when I'm angry, but... I mean, lately, some days I wake up and I just feel like I'm finally, truly awake, you know? Like I'm the only one meant to fix everything going wrong at the facility. But then Mark—my husband—or one of the nurses will tell me to slow down or take a break, and I just snap at them. I get so irritable because it feels like they're just getting in the way, blocking something really important that I have to do. 

Mark has always been like that, though, always telling me to take it easy. He’s the kind of guy who can just sit in his recliner all Sunday watching golf. I don't understand how anyone can watch golf on television. It's just whispering and grass. And the outfits they wear, those pastel polo shirts? Mark bought a salmon-colored one last year for a barbecue at his brother's house, and I told him it washed him out completely. He’s got that pale, kind of ruddy complexion, you know? He burns so easily in the sun. We went to Myrtle Beach a few years ago, and he fell asleep on the sand for an hour without sunscreen. He was peeling for weeks. I had to go to the drugstore and buy three bottles of that green aloe vera gel. The gel is so sticky, though, it ruined the hotel sheets. The hotel tried to charge us a cleaning fee, and I had to argue with the manager at the front desk for twenty minutes. I told him it was a medical necessity, but he just kept pointing at the policy... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, about being angry. Yeah, I snap at people when they tell me to slow down, but the voices from the vents don't really sound different because of it.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits persistent delusions of a specific type (believing voices from vents and speakers are providing accurate information about patient records) without a full manic or depressive episode, which aligns more closely with a diagnosis of persistent delusional disorder.
